blocks.title: Core Concepts
blocks.text: 1. DEFINITION OF Cell cycle: The sequence of events by which cells replicate their genome, grow and divide to form daughter cells is called the cell cycle.

blocks.title: Core Concepts: Cell Cycle /Mitosis
blocks.text:
$G_o$ phase: In adult organisms, some cells do not divide and exit from G₁ stage and enter in the quiescent phase of the cell cycle. e.g., Heart cells.
• Mainly suspended the cell cycle
      • Cells are metabolically active
      • No cell division
      • Cell enter in Go phase at the end of G₁ phase.

blocks.title: Points to remember
blocks.text:
Point to be remember→

1. Mitosis takes place in both haploid and diploid cells.

2. Longest stage of karyokinesis-prophase.

3. The shortest stage of mitosis-anaphase.

4. Chromosomes move toward opposite poles due to the shortening of spindle fibres.

5. Chromosome number becomes just double in anaphase.

6.: Centromere division takes place in the anaphase stage of mitosis.

blocks.title: Exercise 1
blocks.question:
Q.1 During which phase(s) of the cell cycle does the amount of DNA in a cell remain at 4C level if the initial amount is denoted as 2C?

(1) G0 and G1                  (2) G1 and S

(3) Only G2                      (4) G2 and M
blocks.answer:
Ans-4

G1 or first growth is followed by S phase or synthesis phase. DNA replication occurs in S phase and DNA amount doubles up, i.e., a cell with 2C DNA in G1 phase will now have 4C DNA. G2 phase is second growth phase where the DNA content remains the same 4C.
options: (1) G0 and G1
(2) G1 and S
(3) Only G2
(4) G2 and M
blocks.prompt: Q.1 During which phase(s) of the cell cycle does the amount of DNA in a cell remain at 4C level if the initial amount is denoted as 2C?

blocks.title: Exercise 2
blocks.question:
Q 2. In the 'S' phase of the cell cycle:

(1) The amount of DNA doubles in each cell.

(2) The amount of DNA remains the same in each cell.

(3) Chromosome number is increased.

(4) The amount of DNA is reduced to half in each cell.
blocks.answer:
Ans-1

  • The S phase (Synthesis phase) of the cell cycle is the period during which DNA replication occurs.
  • During this phase, the amount of DNA doubles, but the chromosome number remains the same. For example, in a human diploid cell, the DNA content increases from 2C to 4C, but the chromosome number remains at 46.
options: (1) The amount of DNA doubles in each cell.
(2) The amount of DNA remains the same in each cell.
(3) Chromosome number is increased.
(4) The amount of DNA is reduced to half in each cell.

blocks.title: Exercise 4
blocks.question:
Q.4 Which one of the following never occurs during mitotic cell division?

(1) Movement of centrioles towards opposite poles

(2) Pairing of homologous chromosomes

(3) Coiling and condensation of the chromatids

(4) Spindle fibres attach to the kinetochores of chromosomes.
blocks.answer:
Ans.2

Pairing of homologous chromosomes never occurs during mitotic cell division.
options: (1) Movement of centrioles towards opposite poles
(2) Pairing of homologous chromosomes
(3) Coiling and condensation of the chromatids
(4) Spindle fibres attach to the kinetochores of chromosomes.

(1) Spindle fibres attach to the centromere of chromosomes.

(2) Chromosomes decondense at telophase.

(3) Splitting of centromere occurs at anaphase.

(4) All the chromosomes lie at the equator at metaphase.

blocks.title: Exercise 6
blocks.question:
Q.6 . The fruit fly has 8 chromosomes (2n) in each cell. During the interphase of Mitosis if the number of chromosomes at the G1 phase is 8; what would be the number of chromosomes after the S-phase?

(1) 8

(2) 16

(3) 4

(4) 32
blocks.answer:
Ans.1

If the number of chromosomes at G1 phase is 8, then the number of chromosomes after S phase also will be 8.

blocks.title: Core Concepts: Meiosis
blocks.text:
Introduction and Definition:

This specialised kind of cell division that reduces the chromosome number by half results in the production of haploid daughter cells. This kind of division is called meiosis.

Meiosis: Reductional division

• Meiosis involves two sequential cycles of nuclear division and cell division but only a single cycle of DNA replication.

blocks.title: Core Concept: Interkinesis
blocks.text:
Interkinesis:

• Stage between meiosis I & II.

• DNA replication does not occur. It is a short-duration phase.

blocks.title: Exercise 2: Meiosis
blocks.question:
Q.2 After meiosis-I, the resultant daughter cells have:
(1) Same amount of DNA as in the parent cell in S phase
(2) Twice the amount of DNA in comparison to haploid gamete.
(3) Same amount of DNA in comparison to haploid gamete
(4) Four times the amount of DNA in comparison to haploid gamete
blocks.answer:
ANS. 2

After meiosis I, the daughter cells have twice the amount of DNA in comparison to haploid gamete

(2) Twice the amount of DNA in comparison to haploid gamete.
(3) Same amount of DNA in comparison to haploid gamete

blocks.question:
Q.3 Crossing over takes place between which chromatids and in which stage of the cell cycle?

(1)  Non- sister chromatids of non- homologus chromosomes at Zygotene stage of prophase I.

(2)  Non- sister chromatids of  homologus chromosomes at Pachytene  stage of prophase I.

(3) Non- sister chromatids of  homologus chromosomes at  Zygotene   stage of prophase I.

(4)  Non- sister chromatids of non- homologus chromosomes at Pachytene   stage of prophase I.
blocks.answer:
Ans- 2

Crossing over takes place between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes during the pachytene stage of prophase I in meiosis.

(2)  Non- sister chromatids of  homologus chromosomes at Pachytene  stage of prophase I.
